item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00334","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C12","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 is expressly identified in the child as the March 1948 directive governing the requested loyalty files. The child reuses its distinctive rationale—protecting investigative effectiveness, confidential sources, and employees from unfounded allegations—and applies its operative rule that loyalty records remain confidential even when demanded by an outside body. C12 concerns the same loyalty program but only incorporates its investigation and review procedures; C06 has a loosely related executive-legislative conflict but no comparable confidentiality machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"In March of 1948, I issued a Directive to all officers and employees in the Executive Branch of the Government, directing that all reports, records, and files relating to the employee loyalty program be kept in strict confidence, even in instances where subpoenas were received.","parent_excerpt":"all reports, records, and files relative to the loyalty of employees or prospective employees ... shall be maintained in confidence ... Any subpena or demand or request for information, reports, or files ... shall be respectfully declined","explanation":"The child explicitly invokes and closely restates C16's central operative command."},{"child_excerpt":"the serious prejudice to the effectiveness of the Federal Bureau of Investigation as an investigative agency, the resulting embarrassment and danger to confidential informants, and injustice and unfairness to innocent individuals","parent_excerpt":"This is necessary in the interest of our national security and welfare, to preserve the confidential character and sources of information furnished, and to protect Government personnel against the dissemination of unfounded or disproved allegations.","explanation":"The child develops the same distinctive three-part justification for confidentiality found in C16."},{"child_excerpt":"bearing in mind at all times my responsibility to take care that the investigative activities and efficiency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and other investigative agencies remain unimpaired, that innocent people ... not be unnecessarily injured","parent_excerpt":"in accordance with the long-established policy that reports rendered by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and other investigative agencies of the executive branch are to be regarded as confidential","explanation":"Both texts employ the same administrative machinery and policy concerns concerning investigative-agency files, informants, and innocent subjects."}]}
